changes.description: named runs by default on ghcr.io/unxwares/bind9:9.20.30 (imageProvider: unxwares): BIND 9.20.30 built by UnxWares from the ISC release tarball, checked against its SHA-256 and ISC's OpenPGP signature, with the build options, paths and user (bind, uid 53) of the official image, rebuilt twice a week on the current Alpine packages. It replaces docker.io/internetsystemsconsortium/bind9:9.20, whose Alpine packages carry 18 fixable high vulnerabilities (the image is only rebuilt at each BIND release); imageProvider: upstream keeps it.

imageProvider now also selects the named image (and the helm test pod image). image.repository is empty by default and an empty image.tag follows the provider: the BIND release (9.20.30, the new appVersion) for the UnxWares image, the branch (9.20) for the ISC image.

nodeSelector is empty by default: the UnxWares image is published for amd64 and arm64. When named runs the ISC image (amd64 only), the chart adds kubernetes.io/arch: amd64 itself, unless nodeSelector sets that key.

Tests: the end-to-end test runs named (and its client pods) on the BIND image of the commit, built in CI; chart-testing installs ci/default-values.yaml on the UnxWares images and ci/upstream-values.yaml on the official ones; unit tests cover the image, tag and node selector of both providers.

changes.description: Kener 4.2.0 moves nodemailer (7 to 10), sharp (0.34 to 0.35, libvips, libheif and librsvg in its prebuilt binaries) and glob (13 to 14, with minimatch 11) past their advisories: npm audit of the production dependencies goes from 2 high and 3 moderate findings to none.

Custom monitor eval code (API, Ping, TCP and GameDig monitors) no longer runs inside the Kener server process, where it could read the container environment (KENER_SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL...), its files and the network, without a time limit. Kener 4.2.1 runs each eval in a QuickJS sandbox compiled to WebAssembly, in its own short-lived Node.js process with only TZ from the environment, stopped after 10 seconds, at most 2 at a time. It works under the chart hardening as is (no writable path, capability or variable added), and the end-to-end test now checks it. Its 256 MB memory limit does not bound the eval process yet: an eval that allocates without bound still gets Kener OOM-killed (see Monitor eval code in the README).

Kener 4.2.1 (from 4.1.11). Eval code that uses Node.js or browser features (fetch, process, require, Buffer, setTimeout, URL, TextDecoder, crypto, Intl) now reports DOWN: review custom evals before upgrading (see Upgrading in the README). Every check of an API, Ping, TCP or GameDig monitor, with the built-in eval too, starts a Node.js process in the Kener container (about 70 MiB plus what the eval allocates, 2 at a time). Recurring maintenances can repeat in a time zone and keep their local time across clock changes (a migration adds a nullable column at the first start), group monitors can list their members inline, and monitors keep honouring HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY with Axios 1.21.
